new_statements.rule_in_words: Baale is described as a register-tone language (three level tones H, M, L; L of restricted distribution; no downdrift), with the tone system explicitly called poorly understood; neither this chapter (no page containing both 'Baale' and 'stress' or 'accent') nor, as far as searchable, the 1998 primary sketch says anything about word stress or accent placement.
new_statements.exceptions: none; the only qualification is that the low tone 'appears to have a limited distribution' and the whole tonal analysis is provisional
new_statements.domain_note: Lexical/word-level tone marking on citation forms (three registers, mid unmarked). No statement at word or phrase level about stress. Evidence that the descriptions are silent on stress comes from full-text index searches (OHAL 2020: 'Baale stress' 0 pages, 'Baale accent' 0 pages; Surmic 1998 volume: 'Baale stress' 0 pages), not from reading the complete sections.
new_statements.identity_note: All sources refer to the same language, kaci1244 / ISO koe (renamed 'Kacipo-Bale Suri' by ISO 639-3 in 2021). 'Baale' (Yigezu & Dimmendaal, Dimmendaal 2020; data collected by Moges Yigezu on the Ethiopian side) and 'Bale' (Moeller 2009, SIL Ethiopia workshop, Ethiopian speakers who also speak Tirma) denote the Ethiopian community; 'Kacipo' (Arensen 1989) is the Boma-plateau (South Sudan) community of the same language; 'Zilmamu' (Bender 1977) is an older exonym. Glottolog lists no dialects under kaci1244. Encyclopaedia Aethiopica entries are filed by Glottolog under bale1254 but describe this language.

sources.citation: Bender, M. Lionel. 1977. The Surma language group: a preliminary report. Studies in African Linguistics, Supplement 7: 11-21.
sources.note: Group-level phonology notes (pp.15-16) discuss tone/stress only for Murle, Mursi, Majang, Bodi, Muguji ('If tone exists, it appears to be correlated with stress and/or length'); Bale/Zilmamu figure only in classification and lexicostatistic tables. No Bale-specific prosodic statement.

sources.citation: Moeller, Mirjam. 2009. Vowel Harmony in Bale: A study of ATR harmony in a Surmic language of Ethiopia. BA thesis, Department of Linguistics, Stockholm University (DiVA diva2:233078). 26 pp.
sources.note: Nothing on stress. p.7: 'Contrastive vowel length and tone were attested but had to be disregarded because of time limitations and will therefore not be treated in this paper. An initial analysis on vowel length, tone and the consonants in Bale has been made by Yigezu and Dimmendaal (1998).' Nine-vowel ATR system, noun suffix harmony only.
